clue.text: Contributor's chat over cold beer in shade

indicators.note: in an across clue 'over' can mean turned over, so the word for chat is read right to left

parts.note: to rap is to talk freely, chat

indicators.note: the cold beer sits inside the shade, held between its letters

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour
C for cold, as on taps
IPA is India Pale Ale, a beer

explanation.surface: Someone at a gathering chats away over a cold beer in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR (rap turned over) then TI(C IPA)NT gives PARTICIPANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A participant takes part and so makes a contribution to an event or discussion.

clue.text: Examine arsenic, for example

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
'say' introduces an example, as in 'a fruit, say'

explanation.surface: A chemist is told to test a sample of arsenic as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'for example' modify arsenic, but it is a separate piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay is to test or analyse a substance, typically metal ore, for its composition.

clue.text: Kitchen features in a quiet university uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters go up the grid, read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
p is piano, the musical marking for quiet
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A campus revolt erupts quietly, with kitchens somehow at the centre of it.
explanation.walkthrough: In orchestral slang the 'kitchen' is the percussion section, not a room for cooking; IN A P MIT read upwards gives TIMPANI.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums, prominent instruments in the percussion section that players nickname the kitchen.

clue.text: Country where miracle happened, around this time

parts.note: at the wedding in Cana Jesus turned water into wine, his first miracle

indicators.note: turned around, the abbreviation for this era runs backwards

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A traveller names the country where a miracle took place at about this time.
explanation.walkthrough: Cana in Galilee is where Jesus turned water into wine; AD is Anno Domini, the label of our own era.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is the large North American nation north of the United States.

clue.text: Not natural to adopt island supported by power of water?

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so one word is taken inside another

parts.note: a posed photograph is artificial, not natural
I is the abbreviation for island
something resting on a base is supported by it

explanation.surface: Something unnatural takes in an island, propped up by hydraulic power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power of water' reads like hydraulics; the question mark signals a playful definition of the sea god.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea, a mighty deity ruling the oceans.

clue.text: Extremely worthy Frenchman's good in retreat — in case

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the French word runs backwards

parts.note: bon is French for good
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: A very worthy Frenchman's virtue backs off, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: BON reversed gives NOB, then LEST: NOBLEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Noblest is the superlative of noble, meaning the most morally worthy or honourable.

clue.text: Philosophy corrupting most of belief in morals

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter
corrupting something spoils its order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: belief without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school of thought is accused of eroding faith in ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoliberalism is a political and economic doctrine favouring free markets and minimal state intervention.

clue.text: Newly designed base on yard light

parts.note: a rest is a support or base
Y is the abbreviation for yard
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: A lamp with a new design sits on a base in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the base comes first; LED stands for light-emitting diode.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restyled has been given a new look or fashioned differently.

clue.text: Writer glad aeroplane gets dismantled

indicators.note: something dismantled is taken apart and could be rebuilt in any order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A happy author watches an aircraft being taken to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was the American author of macabre tales and poems such as The Raven.

clue.text: Moon reflected across southern town

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front
lying across something means spanning it, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to moon about is to mope listlessly
S for southern

explanation.surface: The moon's light is reflected across a town in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moon' looks like a noun but is the verb to mope; EPOM goes round S to give EPSOM, a Surrey town famous for its Derby racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a market town in Surrey, south of London, home to the Derby horse race.

clue.text: Fall of red and black football team, shortly after return of English Spurs player

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: E for English
Son Heung-min played for Tottenham Hotspur, known as Spurs

indicators.note: cut short, the team name loses its final letter

parts.note: B for black, as on pencils
Leeds United, a football club

explanation.surface: A red-and-black football side slips down the table, behind a Spurs star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall of red' reads like a club's decline but is blood falling. NOSE (E SON reversed) then B and LEED(S): NOSEBLEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebleed is a flow of blood from the nostrils, literally red liquid falling.

clue.text: Consultancy breaking 50-50 with two making common border

indicators.note: breaking into something means entering its middle

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral 50, twice
EY, formerly Ernst & Young, is a consultancy firm
with and 'and' both join things
II is the Roman numeral two

explanation.surface: Consultants split a deal evenly while two of them settle a boundary dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: L(EY)L then AND and II. Leylandii are fast-growing conifers much planted as garden hedges in Britain, and a famous cause of neighbour disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: Leylandii conifers are planted widely as hedges, so they form a very common garden boundary.

clue.text: More times: time within time

indicators.note: within means placed inside, so these pieces go into the last word

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
x is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'
T for time

explanation.surface: A request for more and more time, nested repetitively.
explanation.walkthrough: X and T go inside ERA: EXTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, an amount beyond the usual, which is what 'more' asks for.

clue.text: Including nothing irrational, pen life story

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the pen goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen
O looks like zero, nothing
pi is the best-known irrational number

explanation.surface: A writer resolves to pen a life story with nothing illogical in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun here: pi. BI(O PI)C.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopic is a biographical film dramatising the life of a real person.

clue.text: Unit gathering about northerly capital again

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so the unit wraps round the rest

parts.note: one is a single unit
c is circa, about

indicators.note: heading north in a down clue means going up the grid, so the city is read upwards

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A military unit rounds up people around a northern capital.
explanation.walkthrough: ON(C EMOR)E, with EMOR being ROME read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Once more is an idiom meaning one more time, repeated, as with 'again'.

clue.text: Law largely restricting work for bread

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so one piece holds the other
largely means mostly, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the Torah is the Jewish Law
to till the soil is to work it

explanation.surface: Legislation largely restricts work done for money, or bread.
explanation.walkthrough: TORA(h) holds TILL: TOR(TILL)A. 'Bread' tempts as slang for money, but it is the flatbread.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin Mexican flatbread made from maize or wheat flour.

clue.text: Somehow, of old, books filled with illumination

indicators.note: somehow suggests being done in an unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
lit is short for literature, books

explanation.surface: Ancient books are somehow full of enlightenment.
explanation.definitionFit: A floodlit building is bathed in strong artificial light from broad lamps.

clue.text: You shouldn't have piercing knife around performances

indicators.note: piercing means going into something, so this piece sits inside the other
turned around, the knife word runs backwards

parts.note: a slicer is a cutting blade
'You shouldn't have!' is a way of saying thanks, and ta is British for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a knife being pushed into them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have!' is what people say on receiving a gift, so it stands for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Recitals are concerts or readings given before an audience, usually by soloists.

clue.text: Tormented with difficulty in severe weather

parts.note: torn by doubts means tormented
ado is fuss or trouble, as in 'without much ado'

explanation.surface: Someone suffers, struggling badly through a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins TORN to ADO here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating column of wind, an extreme form of storm.

clue.text: Reported restraint of one making vows

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by speech, so we go by sound

parts.note: a bridle is the headgear that restrains a horse

explanation.surface: News of a restriction placed on someone taking vows.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal describes things belonging to a bride, the person exchanging wedding promises.

clue.text: Struggle to get on a dog after resistance

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
taken as written
to dog someone is to follow or trace them

explanation.surface: Climbing onto a dog proves hard after some resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after resistance' puts R first, then A and TRACE. 'Dog' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the competitive scramble of working life, everyone fighting to get ahead.

clue.text: Trojan cow

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the greatest hero of Troy in the Iliad
second meaning: a verb, to bully or intimidate

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trojan cow' suggests some wooden-horse variant; 'cow' is the verb to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan prince of Homer's Iliad bears the name, and as a verb it means to bully or browbeat.

clue.text: Triple murderer's sheltering Madagascan?

indicators.note: sheltering means keeping inside, so the answer sits within the letters of the words

parts.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A killer of three is protecting someone from Madagascar.
explanation.walkthrough: tripLE MURderer's. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates found in the wild only on Madagascar, so one is a typical native.

clue.text: Prepare too much in public shower?

parts.note: overt means open, done in public view
a shower is a fall of rain

explanation.surface: Someone overdoes their preparations under a downpour in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrain is to exercise excessively when getting ready for a competition, harming performance.

clue.text: First lady's partner's the president

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, was partnered with Adam
the possessive ending supplies its letter

explanation.surface: The First Lady's husband is the President.
explanation.walkthrough: First Lady suggests a president's wife, but here she is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were both presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Burn a lot of paper, with permit on the way

parts.note: St is street, a way
a ream is 500 sheets of paper
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: Someone burns a stack of paper, having been allowed to on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' looks like setting fire, but it is the Scottish word for a stream; 'on' places the paper and permit after the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamlet is a small stream, which in Scotland and northern England is called a burn.

clue.text: Fashionable to skip Delaware massacre site

indicators.note: skipping something means leaving it out, so those letters vanish

parts.note: à la mode means in fashion
DE is the postal abbreviation for Delaware

explanation.surface: A trendy traveller bypasses Delaware to visit a historic battleground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo, a mission in San Antonio, Texas, was where Mexican forces killed its defenders in 1836.

clue.text: Doctor greets pilot, noisy one who's departed?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A medic welcomes an aviator, while a rowdy passenger has just left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person greeting, but it is a verb. 'departed' hints at the dead, not a passenger leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A poltergeist is a ghost said to make loud bangs and throw objects about, a spirit of the dead.
